Variation No.3 to the County Development Plan 2021 - 2027  
Notice is hereby given that Laois County Council, in accordance with Section 58 of the 
Planning and Development Act 2024 and 2025, proposes to make a variation 
(hereinafter referred to as "the Proposed Variation No.3") to the Laois County 
Development Plan 2021 – 2027 (hereafter referred to as ‘the Plan’). The Proposed 
Variation will be incorporated into Volume 1 and Volume 2 of the Plan. 
 
The proposed variation to the Plan is intended to address specific, immediate policy 
updates that are needed in the short term and proposes to: 
• 
Amend a number of sections in the Volume 1 (Written Statement) including:  
• 
Chapter’s 4, 5, 8, 12, 13, 14 
• 
Include additional policies including nature based solutions, public services 
and large scale residential development 
 
• 
Mapping changes setting out:  
• 
Proposed rezonings and the addition of residential zoned lands at 
approximately 25no. settlements in response to the Ministerial Guidelines. 
• 
Amend the Roads Objective and Buffer at Portlaoise and Abbeyleix 
 
• 
Amend a number of sections in the Volume 2 (Settlement Strategy)  
• 
Include an additional RPS in Appendix 1  
 
The Proposed Variation is accompanied by:  
• 
A Residential Audit  
• 
A Site Assessment Report  
• 
A Strategic Flood Risk Assessment of the proposed zoning amendments 
• 
An Appropriate Assessment (AA) Natura Impact Report and associated AA 
Screening Determination, pursuant to the EU Habitats Directive (92/43/EEC) and 
Planning and Development Act 2024 (as amended),  
• 
A Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) Environmental Report and 
associated SEA Screening Determination pursuant to the European SEA Directive 
(2001/42/EC) and the European Union (Land Use Planning – SEA) Regulations 
2025  
• 
An assessment of the proposed Record of Protected Structure

(both dates inclusive) at the following locations:

Strategic Infrastructure Development Application by Dara Energy Limited 
 
Under Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended) - Notice of Direct Planning 
Application to An Coimisiún Pleanála in respect of a Strategic Infrastructure 
Development, within the Local Administrative Boundaries of County Kildare, County 
Offaly and County Laois. In accordance with section 37E of the Planning and 
Development Act 2000 (as amended), has been lodged. 
 
Dara Energy Limited made an application to An Coimisiún Pleanála (the “Commission”) 
for permission for a period of 10 years, for development comprising the construction 
and operation of a wind farm and related works within the townlands of Kilbeggan South, 
Hallsfarm, Stonehouse Farm; Ballybought, Durrow Demesne, Aghancarnan, Gormagh, 
Acantha, Ballynasrah or Tinnycross, Ardan, Puttaghan, Cappancur, Cloncollog, 
Meelaghans, Annagharvey, Ballycollin, Ballina, Ballyknockan, Ballymooney, Ballycue, 
Ballinagar, Knockballyboy, Clonad, Townparks, Castlebarnagh Big, Killoneen, Killeen, 
Esker Beg, Ballycon, Drumcaw or Mountlucas, Derrycricket, Ballaghassaan, Walshisland, 
Bunnagappagh, Coolagary, Raheenakeeran, Enaghan, Moanvane, Cushina, Clonsast 
Lower, and Chevychase or Derrynadarragh in County Offaly; Aughrim and Derrylea in 
County Kildare; and Inchacooly, Coolnaferagh, Ullard or Controversyland, Clonanny, Lea, 
Loughmansland Glebe, and Bracklone in County Laois.  
 
This development is covered by the provisions of the Renewable Energy Directive III 
(Directive 2023/2413) and the planning application is subject to a completeness check 
under section 37JA of the Planning and Development Act 2000, as amended. The 
proposal is considered a ‘Renewable Energy Development’ under the definition 
introduced by S.I. 274 of 2025 into Section 2 of the Planning and Development Act 
2000, as amended. When a notice issues in accordance with section 37JA(b), the 
provisions of article 26A of the Planning and Development Regulations 2001 to 2025 
shall apply.  
 
The development is a renewable energy development and will consist of a 10-year 
permission and a 35-year operational life from the date of commissioning of the entire 
Wind Farm. Any submissions/observations must be accompanied by a fee of €50 (except 
for certain prescribed bodies) and must be received by the Commission not later than 
5:30 p.m. on 2nd April 2026

Economic Development Visit to Liverpool  
 
On the 17th – 18th February, A delegation (Ms. McEvoy, DOS Economic Development and Mr. 
Reddin A/ Head of LEO and Cllr James Kelly Chair of the Economic development SPC )  attended 
meetings with Reps from the Economic and Enterprise Section, Carlow County Council, SETU 
and Paul Radcliffe & Rob March from Liverpool Enterprise Regions.

The trip included visits to  
 
• 
Baltic Ventures: 
A flagship early-stage tech accelerator in the Liverpool City Region. Creating an environment 
where being based outside of London is no disadvantage to emerging technology companies. 
They offer “Launchpad” which is Liverpool City Region’s 12-week programme for ambitious 
founders ready to turn ideas into impact. Gain hands-on workshops, expert 1:1 coaching, 
and a supportive founder community. 
 
• 
CENTRAL TECH at Sciontec | Liverpool's New Tech Hub 
CENTRAL TECH offers a collaborative community environment, where businesses engaged 
in technology and digitalisation can thrive, including those specifically working within 
advanced manufacturing technologies, sustainability, sensors and the Internet of Things. The 
building benefits from being part of the LCR Connect digital infrastructure, providing a full-
fibre, ultrafast, gigabit-capable network for customers, to access next-generation future-
proofed and cloud enabled technologies.  This trip offered the opportunity to visit centres 
similar to the Connected Hubs and review what the new emerging businesses are and how 
challenges are being met in terms of turning ideas into impact.  
Local Enterprise Week 2026 
Small businesses, entrepreneurs and aspiring start-ups across the county took part in 15 
events delivered as part of Laois Local Enterprise Week 2026, which ran from 2–6 March, 
offering practical supports, expert insights and networking opportunities to help businesses 
start, grow and thrive.  Local Enterprise Week is a national initiative of the Local Enterprise 
Offices, supported by Enterprise Ireland and local authorities, and once again saw strong 
engagement in Laois, with a diverse programme open to businesses at every stage. While 
hundreds of events took place nationwide during the week, Laois Local Enterprise Office 
delivered a packed schedule of in-person events, talks and mentoring clinics tailored to local 
needs.

Student Enterprise Awards 2026 
Local Enterprise Office Laois are delighted to announce that teenage entrepreneurs from St 
Mary`s CBS, Portlaoise & Scoil Chríost Ri, Portlaoise will represent Laois at this year’s Student 
Enterprise Programme National Finals on Thursday 7th May.  
The students all took part in the Laois Final on 10th March, which was held at the Midlands Park 
Hotel, Portlaoise.   More than 750 students from 9 schools took part in the annual programme 
locally.  
The enterprise education initiative, funded by the Government of Ireland through Enterprise 
Ireland and delivered by the 31 Local Enterprise Offices in local authorities throughout the 
country, saw over 30,000 students from just under 500 secondary schools across the country 
take part in 2025 / 2026. The programme supports students to create, design and market their 
own business, all with the hope of reaching the National Finals.  
In the Junior Category of the competition, Laois will be represented at the National Finals by 
Paddy Lynch & Tom McDonald from ‘I-CAN” at St Mary`s CBS.  
In the Intermediate Category of the competition, Laois will be represented at the National Finals 
by Abbie Holmes & Emma White from “Solas Seunóga” at Scoil Chríost Rí  
 
In the Senior Category of the competition, Laois will be represented on May 7th by James Doody, 
Harry Ramsbottom & Alex Delaney from “DRD Balespikes” at St Mary`CBS

Pathways to “Progress: Real Stories, Real Impact.”

Bosca Beo 
Laois and Longford County Councils recently unveiled Bosca Beo, an innovative project 
designed to help people record, collect, cherish, and share their life memories with loved 
ones.  Developed collaboratively by the Creative Ireland, Age Friendly, Library Services, 
and Healthy Ireland teams in both local authorities, Bosca Beo takes the form of a 
beautifully illustrated memory box, styled after a vintage suitcase. Inside, there is space 
to safely store keepsakes, photographs, documents, and other important personal items. 
The box contains a set of 80 prompt cards with gentle questions to help spark memories 
and conversations. These cards are ideal for sharing stories with family members of all 
ages, making it a wonderful intergenerational activity. Included is a life journal where 
people can write about their experiences, from childhood through to the present day.  
In addition, Bosca Beo includes a family tree booklet, allowing users to record details 
about themselves and previous generations, helping to preserve their family history for 
the future. The H.S.E. are to conduct a trial programme in a care setting in Laois, using 
the Bosca Beo to increase activity, stimulate conversation and create a bond between 
staff and residents. They will report back on their findings following the trial.

transatlantic flight in history.  This crew included Laois man Colonel James Fitzmaurice

with the Col. Fitzmaurice Committee and a number of national stakeholders to plan the 
centenary commemoration of this historic event in 2028.  The objective in 2026 is to 
engage a suitable company to:

2. Plan a programme of events for the centenary in 2028.
